second_order: rallying able-bodied clickers to make a Patriots mark
theme_note: These passages share the practice of calling Patriots people into a build and answering that call; they vary from invitations and volunteering to offering accounts, challenging non-participation, and asking for a sticky or more numbers.

second_order: working out the outline, timer, and fill
theme_note: These passages coordinate the immediate craft of the first logo: choosing an outline, explaining the five-minute effort and location, and prioritising how to fill it.

second_order: making room with neighbouring pixelers
theme_note: These codes hold together because participants negotiate how the Patriots build and VLK can occupy nearby space without fighting; what varies is whether they announce the truce, request temporary filling help, warn against interference, promise restraint, or report progress.

second_order: watching the flying Elvis get noticed, changed, and lost
theme_note: These passages monitor an unstable emblem across its visible life: noticing attention or danger, reporting defacement and unfinished work, claiming random colours, and mourning its disappearance.

second_order: staging Patriots April Fools and seeing who falls for it
theme_note: These codes share the room practice of preparing, posting, extending, testing, rejecting, recognising, and admitting reactions to Patriots April Fools claims; they vary from small fake trades and images to a moderator-led NFL ban hoax.

second_order: rallying the Watchers to defend the Pats pixel wall
theme_note: These passages share the practice of turning threats, encroachment, or damage into calls and shifts for defenders; they vary from asking for backup and switching to damage control to reporting for duty, touching up pixels, and naming the wall watch.

second_order: moving the build talk into Discord
theme_note: This passage creates an off-platform organising room and recruits moderators for it, moving part of the build work beyond the visible thread.

second_order: having AutoModerator block place recruitment links
theme_note: This passage records the room configured link rule interrupting an r/place recruitment call, a moderation practice distinct from either building or answering the call.

second_order: claiming the scoreboard as our mark
theme_note: These passages publicly represent the Patriots through the scoreboard and celebrate or claim its completion; they vary from calling it the room’s mark to praising the builders and the triumph it depicts.

second_order: calling for taking out rival marks
theme_note: These posts recruit people to overwrite a Fins logo rather than maintain the Patriots work; repetition across near-duplicate calls makes the attack practice visible.

second_order: telling would-be attackers to leave the Fins logo
theme_note: This reply resists the attack call and substitutes a rainbow connection, drawing a participant boundary around what not to destroy.

second_order: giving up on a Patriots logo on the Swedish flag
theme_note: This passage closes a side build by explicitly abandoning it; it belongs with no other practice in the slice and is kept as a single-code theme.

second_order: standing down when placement is over
theme_note: This passage ends active defence by telling participants the event is over and to stop, a closure practice distinct from celebrating the result afterward.

second_order: explaining r/place as collaborative pixel making
theme_note: This passage teaches a newcomer what the event is and frames it as people collaborating one pixel at a time; it is explanatory conduct rather than building, defending, or commemorating.

second_order: celebrating that the scoreboard survived to the end
theme_note: These closing turns congratulate the room and claim survival with the scoreboard intact at the moment placement ended.

second_order: laughing at the neighbour doughnut logo after closure
theme_note: This post-event reply turns from late warnings to joking about a neighbouring design; no other pooled code performs this specific practice.

second_order: recounting how the scoreboard was defended and who helped
theme_note: These closing comments reconstruct the work behind the surviving scoreboard: continual repairs, repelling incursions, help from neighbouring communities, broadened credit beyond Patriots fans, and the mix of scripts and people. What varies is the actor credited and the kind of help remembered.

second_order: proposing the nuclear option of recruiting r/the_donald
theme_note: This proposal recruits a particular outside group as a nuclear option and belongs with no other pooled practice.

second_order: sharing and reworking the final place images
theme_note: These codes circulate, improve, watch, and appraise final images and a timelapse after placement; they vary from making a cleaned version to mourning its absence, compressing a night into seconds, and sharing favourite finds.

second_order: planning what to draw if r/place restarts
theme_note: These proposals carry the finished event forward by choosing what the room might draw next time; they vary between updating and immortalising the scoreboard and replacing it with an Edelcatch mural.

second_order: arguing whether bots and scripts belong in collaboration
theme_note: These replies debate the means of a future build: captcha against bots, confidence or doubt about competing with them, admission of scripting, insistence on human placement, script-writing as collaboration, and distributing a script template.
